title: How stitches work when doctors actually use them

hook.narration: When doctors sew you up, the most important thread never surfaces.

visual.pose: skygawk (surgeon hero tiny at frame edge, curious lean)
visual.prop: skin cross-section OWNS the frame: cream epidermis band, amber thread arcing UNDER the surface with 3-stop glow, teal needle tip entering; NO text on frame-0 (L-109: the image poses the question)

fact_sources: running subcuticular (intradermal) suture lies entirely WITHIN the dermis and never surfaces; first described by Halsted (Zhang, Xie & Zeng, Dermatol Surg 2022, PMC9154294); 'leaves behind practically no suture mark on the skin' (Chatterjee 2012, PubMed)

scenes.narration: Forget the shoelace picture: loops and knots on top.

visual.prop: MYTH frame: surface sutures as ink loops + knots ON the cream band, dimmed and cracking = the old picture; hero steps back

fact_sources: belief frame: simple interrupted sutures with visible knots are one common closure, but the flat-scar closures run subcuticularly (PMC9154294) — the scene presents the assumption being corrected, not a false fact

scenes.narration: For scars that heal flat, the thread rides under the surface.

visual.prop: thread path animates beneath the bright surface line (arc wipe follows the needle path), wound edges below start to meet

fact_sources: subcuticular suture proven to reduce scar width via tension reduction on wound edges (PMC9154294)

scenes.narration: It's the subcuticular stitch: one thread hidden inside the skin.

visual.prop: STAMP 'SUBCUTICULAR' (cream chip, ink stroke on busy zone) + thread highlighted inside the dermis band

fact_sources: technique name and lineage (PMC9154294) — the name lives in the STAMP (ASR cannot carry it, day-013 precedent); VO says it

scenes.narration: The needle zigzags through one layer, catching both edges every pass.

visual.prop: NEEDLE CLOSE-UP OWNS the frame: teal needle zigzagging through the amber dermis band, entry/exit bites marked on both wound edges; scatter-angle arc wipe = G9 hero moment (reuse #0003 device)

fact_sources: running intradermal stitch passes horizontally through the dermis taking a small bite on each side of the wound (subcuticular technique teaching, limbsandthings suture tutor; Halsted lineage PMC9154294)

scenes.narration: Each pass pulls the gap shut: a zipper under the surface.

visual.prop: wound gap closes from below as the thread 'zipper' pulls: two skin edges slide together, ink dash zipper line abstract under the surface

fact_sources: continuous intradermal suture apposes wound edges as it runs (subcuticular technique teaching, limbsandthings)

scenes.narration: The end knot gets buried, where your skin swallows it whole.

visual.prop: camera dives to the KNOT: ink knot tucked beneath the dermis band, gentle closing motion around it, teal rim on the needle tail

fact_sources: most subcuticular closures use absorbable sutures that are not removed, secured with a buried knot technique (limbsandthings suture tutor); knotless running variants also documented (ISHS 'running subcutaneous suture without knots') — VO says 'buried', never 'no knots at all'

scenes.narration: No stitch tracks. Just a clean seam.

visual.prop: compare frame: railroad-track stitch marks (myth side, dimmed) vs the clean surface line (glowing faint)

fact_sources: 'practically no suture mark on the skin' (Chatterjee 2012, PubMed)

scenes.narration: The thread dissolves on its own. No removal visit.

visual.prop: thread dissolving into drifting amber particles (secondary motion), dermis band calm

fact_sources: most subcuticular closures now use absorbable sutures that are not removed (limbsandthings suture tutor)

scenes.narration: In about two days, the surface seals itself.

visual.prop: surface seals with a gentle pulse along the line; STAMP 'SEALED IN 48 HOURS' lands (digits on-screen legal; VO says words)

fact_sources: well-approximated wounds can re-epithelialize within 48 hours (StatPearls 'Physiology, Epithelialization', NBK532977) — DEVIATION from boss brief's 'CLOSED IN 24 HOURS' recorded in script.md: no source supports 24 h, 48 h is the sourced figure

scenes.narration: The best-stitched skin shows almost no trace.

visual.prop: skin smooth, the faint seam line fading to almost invisible; one restrained sparkle

fact_sources: 'practically no suture mark on the skin' (Chatterjee 2012); RCT cosmesis: patients preferred subcuticular closure for better cosmetic results (Tanaka 2014, PubMed 24439741)

scenes.narration: The finest seam is the one you never see.

visual.prop: loop mirror: same cross-section as hook, thread now dissolved, only the smooth surface + faint seam remain; kinetic closer title pops = the spoken line

fact_sources: one closer (L-077), loops to hook (day-013 structure law); no new claim

visual.prop: closer hold: smooth skin + faint seam shimmer continues, title stays; visual-only pacing beat for L-097 headroom (day-015/#0005 precedent)
